title.narrative: Provide comprehensive WASH, and Shelter/NFI rapid response interventions to mitigate morbidity and mortality among children and their families in response to the Sudan crisis

description.narrative: ltpgtHumanitarian needs continue to increase to alarming levels across Sudan as conflict persists and spreads to new areas. The crisis is causing unprecedented levels of human displacement, food insecurity, damage to critical infrastructure and facilities including WASH and shelter infrastructure, collapse of banking and financial services, and widespread looting. In addition to the ongoing need for large scale humanitarian response activities, there is a widespread recognition among humanitarian actors that there is also a need for rapid response capacity to address rapid onset crisis. ltbrgtIn response to the current SHF funding allocation, SC proposes a project that will deliver WASH and Shelter NFI response activities within 48 hours or a rapid onset crisis. SC is currently implementing the second iteration of the SHF-funded 48 hours response project and the design of this new project is based on learning from the previous phases. Under the current program SC has collaborated with 17 NGOs (7 INGO and 10 NNGO) to respond rapidly and effectively to sudden humanitarian needs across Sudan. INFO partners to date include ACTED, ALIGHT, SOS Sahel, IMC UK, IAS, Solidarites International (SI) and WR. NNGO partners to date include UPO, SOR, Mutawinat, AORD, ADD, SADAGAAT, CAFA, AAO, RDN, and VNRHD.ltbrgtThe proposed project seeks to improve access to safe water, sanitation, and hygiene knowledge for approximately 175,093 individuals. The WASH strategic response encompasses two key components: ltbrgt(i) WASH at the community level: This component includes a 48-hour rapid response capability to address urgent WASH needs. Activities under this involve water trucking, distribution of hygiene kits, hygiene promotion, water quality monitoring, waste management, construction/rehabilitation of emergency latrines, and quick rehabilitation of water yards and hand pumps. In addition, the project will rehabilitate water yards and hand pumps. The rehabilitation will include the integration of solar systems to ensure a cost-effective and environmentally sustainable water supply.ltbrgt(ii) Institutional WASH Activities: In response to specific emergencies, such as cholera outbreaks, the project will implement WASH interventions in institutional settings, including health, nutrition, and educational facilities. These interventions will ensure that these institutions are equipped with necessary WASH infrastructure and materials, including water purification systems, excreta disposal facilities, cleaning materials, and solid waste management systems.ltbrgt(iii) Shelter, NFIs: ltbrgtaims to provide lifesaving shelter and NFI assistance to newly displaced populations, reaching approximately 42,000 individuals. By addressing critical shelter and NFI needs, the intervention will enhance living conditions while mitigating health and protection vulnerabilities.ltbrgtKey activities include the distribution of in-kind emergency shelter kits (ESKs), such as tents, the establishment of communal centers, and rehabilitation of shelters affected by floods. The project will also distribute essential NFIs, including blankets, sleeping mats, plastic sheets, mosquito nets, kitchen sets, and solar lamps, alongside partial NFI kits tailored to specific needs.ltbrgtThe initiative will further focus on improving IDP gathering sites through interventions like backfilling, drainage systems, and lighting. It will provide cash-for-shelter support, facilitate voluntary returns, and promote safe shelter practices through disaster risk reduction (DRR) and participatory approach for safe shelter awareness (PASSA) training to enhance community resilience by equipping individuals with the skills to identify and mitigate shelter-related risks, leading to safer, more disaster-resilient housing.ltbrgtlt/pgt
